checksum_mismatch.verdict: STILL NOT INDUCIBLE through the twelve operations, re-established rather than inherited
checksum_mismatch.evidence: All twelve operations enumerated from contracts/api/v1/openapi.json; no request body of any write operation accepts a sha256, checksum, digest, etag or content-md5 field, so a caller cannot declare a digest at all. The guard itself was proved real at the storage layer: handing S3BlobStore bytes with a false digest raises ChecksumMismatchError (storage_integrity_error) and with a false size raises SizeMismatchError, while the same bytes with their true digest and size publish.

items.summary: driver.REPOSITORY_ROOT.parents[2] is an unguarded index. Any checkout two or fewer levels below / raises IndexError: 2 at fixture setup, so all five live tests ERROR rather than run or skip. /root/w5cert and /root/w5adv are both such paths, and the dispatch itself instructs sessions to use a path under /root/. Where it does not crash it resolves to / rather than to the parent checkout it is documented to find, so the fallback has never worked.
items.impact: criterion 4's live requirement is unreachable from a dispatched worktree at the depth the dispatch prescribes
items.worked_around_by: performing the live run from a second checkout of the same commit at /root/certrun/w5deep, with the suite unmodified

items.summary: The provider configuration is built from dict(os.environ) rather than from the environ mapping create_app was given, overriding only AUDITMANAGER_PROVIDER_MODE. AppSettings.run_cost_ceiling_usd is therefore written at settings.py:139 and read nowhere; the OD-03 ceiling actually in force is re-read independently by load_provider_config. Two resolutions of one ceiling that can disagree.
items.evidence: AUDITMANAGER_RUN_COST_CEILING_USD=0.01 through create_app(environ=...): settings reported 0.01, the stage recorded cost_ceiling_usd 1.0, and the run PUBLISHED having spent 0.038775. The same value in the process environment: run failed with terminal_reason cost_budget_exceeded, publishing nothing.
items.impact: not a journey-level violation in a normal deployment, where one environment feeds both paths. It breaks the composition root's stated contract that create_app(environ=...) composes from that mapping, and it means any future test that sets the ceiling through build_client would be silently vacuous. tests/conftest.py:30 strips the name for the whole session, so nothing in the suite would have caught it.
